title: Commissioning: first contact after separation
summary: Your CubeSat has just left the rocket. It is tumbling, its solar arrays are folded and nobody has talked to it yet.
goals: Understand why a satellite tumbles after separation
Deploy the solar arrays and point them at the Sun
prerequisites: Satellite Builder: build the Academy-3U CubeSat
situation: Separation was 20 minutes ago. The satellite is spinning at several degrees per second with its arrays stowed and its automatic detumble disabled for this test. It will rise over the Baku ground station soon. Each pass lasts only about 10 minutes, so plan what you send.

steps.text: Wait for the first contact (AOS) with the ground station.
steps.hint: Watch 'Ground contact' and the pass timer at the top. Commands can only be sent while in contact.

steps.text: Start detumbling: send ADCS MODE DETUMBLE.
steps.hint: Attitude panel > MODE > DETUMBLE. The magnetorquers push against Earth's magnetic field (B-dot).

steps.text: Wait until the rotation rate drops below 1 deg/s.
steps.hint: This takes several minutes. Use time warp. Detumbling works without contact - it is onboard software.
If the pass is over, wait for the next one - or store the command: OBSW SCHEDULE_IN 60 str.hdrm DEPLOY (must be sent while in contact).

steps.text: Get into SUNSAFE: arrays pointing at the Sun.
steps.hint: After detumbling the software switches to SUNSAFE by itself; otherwise send ADCS MODE SUNSAFE.
'Net power' must be positive in sunlight.

failText: The battery ran flat before the arrays were deployed.
successText: Commissioning complete: the satellite is stable, deployed and power-positive.
